children: China extended its suspension of export restrictions on some critical materials to the U.S., just days after top leaders from the two countries met in the tech hub of Shenzhen.

The Chinese Commerce Ministry on Tuesday said it will continue to halt the export ban on dual-use items related to gallium, germanium, antimony and superhard materials to the U.S. It will also continue to ease stricter reviews on graphite exports to the U.S., according to an official statement.
The decisions, effective Nov. 28, 2026 to Jan. 27, 2027, would prolong a suspension due to expire Friday.

China first suspended these restrictions last November as part of a trade truce reached between the world's two largest economies a year ago. In recent weeks, Beijing and Washington have acted to extend previous agreements, with both sides announcing continued pauses on tariffs and trade curbs.

The extended suspension comes on the heels of last week's Shenzhen summit between President Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping. It also comes less than a day after the U.S. president helped secure the reinstatement of Nvidia Chief Executive Jensen Huang, a vocal critic of strict chip export controls.

Despite these suspensions in place, the trade truce is widely viewed as fragile. Washington's export controls on advanced AI chips to China continue to strain a bilateral relationship dogged by the scandal centered around Huang.
